subject: psychiatry
title: Delirium: Clinical Features, Diagnostic Criteria, and Bedside Management

steps.tx: **Delirium**, an acute confusional state, is characterized by a disturbance in attention and awareness that develops rapidly over hours to days, represents a marked change from baseline, and tends to fluctuate in severity throughout the day. It is an acute manifestation of diffuse cerebral dysfunction caused by underlying medical illness.
steps.say: Delirium is an acute disturbance in attention and awareness developing over hours to days and fluctuating throughout the day, driven by medical illness.

vis.alt: Bedside cognitive domains and clinical assessment of attention in acute delirium
vis.caption: Bedside cognitive domains and clinical assessment of attention in acute delirium.

steps.tx: **Inattention and fluctuating consciousness** represent the foundational diagnostic pillars of delirium. Patients cannot sustain, focus, or shift attention, demonstrated on bedside examination by inability to repeat five digits forwards, perform serial sevens, or spell the word 'WORLD' backwards, characteristically worsening during nighttime hours.
steps.say: Inattention is the core feature of delirium, tested by reciting serial sevens or spelling WORLD backwards, fluctuating markedly from morning to night.

vis.title: Bedside Inattention Testing
rows: Cannot repeat 4 digits; loses focus immediately
Stops, wanders, or repeats forward sequence
Tap hand whenever letter 'A' is read
Frequent errors of omission and commission

steps.tx: **Sundowning** refers to the pronounced exacerbation of confusion, perceptual illusions, and psychomotor agitation occurring in the late afternoon and evening hours as ambient lighting fades. Loss of familiar sensory cues, fatigue, and circadian rhythm disruption combine to trigger terrifying visual misperceptions and restless wandering.
steps.say: Sundowning involves worsening confusion and visual misperceptions in the late afternoon as ambient light fades, disrupting circadian orientation.

left.title: Sundowning Triggers
points: Fading ambient daylight and casting shadows
Fatigue and sensory deprivation at dusk
Hospital shift changes and unfamiliar staff

right.title: Environmental Remedies
points: Visible wall clocks and large calendars
Minimize nocturnal noise and vital sign checks

steps.tx: **Confusion Assessment Method**, abbreviated CAM, is the gold standard validated bedside diagnostic algorithm for delirium, requiring the presence of features 1 and 2, plus either feature 3 or feature 4. Feature 1 requires acute onset and fluctuating course; Feature 2 requires inattention; Feature 3 requires disorganized thinking; Feature 4 requires altered consciousness.
steps.say: The Confusion Assessment Method confirms delirium when acute fluctuating onset and inattention are present alongside disorganized thinking or altered consciousness.

vis.alt: Neurobiological causes and multimodal non-pharmacological management of delirium
vis.caption: Neurobiological causes and multimodal non-pharmacological management of delirium.

steps.tx: **Hypoactive delirium** is characterized by decreased psychomotor activity, lethargy, psychomotor slowing, apathy, and stupor, occurring more frequently than the agitated hyperactive subtype. Crucially, hypoactive delirium carries a significantly worse prognosis and higher mortality because it is frequently misdiagnosed as depression.
steps.say: Hypoactive delirium presents with lethargy, psychomotor slowing, and withdrawal, carrying higher mortality because it is misdiagnosed as depression.

vis.title: Delirium Motor Subtypes
rows: Easily recognized; lower mortality; treated with haloperidol
Frequently missed; highest mortality; avoid sedatives
Alternates between hyperactive agitation and lethargy
Common in ICU; requires dynamic clinical titration

steps.tx: **Etiological evaluation of delirium** demands systematic medical investigation for underlying systemic insults, remembered by the classic clinical mnemonic I WATCH DEATH: Infections, Withdrawal, Acute metabolic, Trauma, CNS pathology, Hypoxia, Deficiencies, Endocrinopathies, Acute vascular, Toxins/drugs, and Heavy metals, requiring comprehensive laboratory screening.
steps.say: Delirium workup investigates systemic causes like sepsis, hypoxia, metabolic collapse, or anticholinergic drugs using the mnemonic I WATCH DEATH.

vis.title: I WATCH DEATH Differential Mnemonic
rows: Pneumonia, urinary tract infection, sepsis, meningitis
Head injury, subdural hematoma, postoperative pain
Stroke, encephalitis, respiratory failure, cardiac arrest

steps.tx: **Electroencephalography in delirium** characteristically demonstrates diffuse, generalized background slowing of cerebral electrical rhythms, characterized by replacement of normal alpha rhythms with prominent theta and delta waves. The sole exception is alcohol or sedative withdrawal delirium, which exhibits fast, low-voltage beta activity.
steps.say: Delirium produces generalized EEG slowing with theta and delta waves, except in alcohol withdrawal which shows fast beta activity.

left.title: General Delirium EEG
points: Prominent theta (4-7 Hz) & delta (<4 Hz) waves
Loss of posterior dominant alpha rhythm

steps.tx: **Pharmacological management with haloperidol** is reserved strictly for severe agitation threatening patient safety or disrupting essential life-saving medical care, administered at low doses (0.5 to 2.0 milligrams orally or intramuscularly). Benzodiazepines are strictly avoided in non-withdrawal delirium because they exacerbate cognitive confusion.
steps.say: Low-dose haloperidol is reserved for severe agitation threatening safety. Benzodiazepines are avoided as they worsen delirium, except in alcohol withdrawal.

vis.title: Delirium Medication Guidelines
rows: High D2 potency; zero anticholinergic effect; monitor QTc
Low D2 binding spares motor function; avoid haloperidol
Replaces deficient GABA-A tone; prevents seizures
Eliminates ammonia; avoid sedatives and narcotics
